title: Ten early GJ 163 fits near 109 days give later HARPS gain ranges that include zero
abstract: We test whether a reported GJ 163 velocity signal near 109 days repeats in later HARPS data. We fit 152 early nightly means from HARPS-RVBank version 02. We keep each early signal fixed and test 49 later nights from 2012 to 2021. The primary 109.745-day wave has an amplitude of 1.683 m/s. It reduces later weighted squared error by 5.13 percent. The 95 percent annual-block range is -22.15 to 20.85 percent. All ten model tests have 30-day and annual-block ranges that include zero. Three spectral-index controls also leave the gain uncertain. An early local loss tolerance of four units permits later point gains from -17.43 to 7.22 percent. A fixed 1.006415-day sampling alias has a lower early loss. Its later gain differs from the long-period gain by 1.21 percentage points, with an annual-block range of -8.71 to 16.00 points. These are conditional tests with fixed early templates. They omit early fit uncertainty and do not supply a planet false-alarm probability. No new planet, physical cause, or independent observation is established. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence, three figures, source hashes, and a retrieval recipe. External measurements stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: All ten model tests give conditional 95 percent ranges that include zero. The point is the later error gain. Blue ranges use 365.25-day blocks. Orange ranges use 30-day blocks. The early signal remains fixed in each resampling test.
A local early period fit can change the sign of the later point gain. A loss tolerance of four units is descriptive. It is not a confidence limit.
The early residual scan and two fitted wave shapes. The later free wave is descriptive. Similar point estimates do not establish a stable planet signal.
